name: Aristotelis Mistakidis
current_role: Private investor; controlling shareholder of Aegean Baltic Bank and majority owner of PAOK BC (via Alpha Sports Group); ex-head of copper at Glencore
profile: Greek-British 'Telis' Mistakidis spent ~25 years at Marc Rich & Co./Glencore after six years trading metals at Cargill, rising to run Glencore's global copper business until 2018; the 2011 IPO made him a billionaire. He now invests in Greek banking (Piraeus, Aegean Baltic Bank), shipping (Union Maritime), real estate and sport.
interesting_fact: In November 2025 he became majority owner of Thessaloniki basketball club PAOK BC, and in 2026 the club announced a new privately operated training centre in Pylaia with two indoor courts.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Rome, where his father, a marine biologist, worked for the United Nations; he told Kathimerini in 2011 that Greek was always spoken at home while he grew up abroad.
notes: Very private; no personal office contact published. Plausible routes: PAOK BC club press office or Aegean Baltic Bank corporate communications. Forbes bio notes a 2018 Canadian regulatory ban—avoid in outreach. Energy/commodities angle (copper, zinc) fits the podcast.

name: Allison McCain
current_role: Chairman, McCain Foods Ltd. (chair since 2004; no 2025-26 source found confirming he still holds the title)
profile: Allison D. McCain, nephew of McCain Foods co-founders Harrison and Wallace McCain, joined the Florenceville, N.B. frozen-potato giant in 1975 as an engineer, ran production in Australia and the UK, became deputy chairman in 1999 and chairman in 2004. His wealth is his family stake in privately held McCain Foods.
interesting_fact: As chair of UNB's 'Forging our Futures' campaign from 2003, he helped raise $107 million, then a record for Atlantic Canada; he later served as UNB's chancellor (named 2013) and chaired the Beaverbrook Art Gallery board.
deep_cut_fact: An electrical engineering graduate of UNB (1972), he worked at the New Brunswick Telephone Company before taking an engineering job at McCain's Florenceville plant in 1975 — the first of the family's next generation to join the firm.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts found. No death reports found (born c.1949). Best route is McCain Foods corporate communications. Only listed by Hurun 2014-2016.

name: Spiro Latsis
current_role: Head of the Latsis family group; chairman of EFG Bank European Financial Group; president of the John S. Latsis Public Benefit Foundation's supervisory board
profile: Spiros J. Latsis (b. 1946) is the son of Greek shipping-and-oil tycoon John S. Latsis (d. 2003) and has led the family's Latsis Group since then. Holdings include EFG International (Swiss private banking), Lamda Development (Athens real estate), a stake in Helleniq Energy and the TALOS shipyard. He also funds the Latsis foundations in Athens and Geneva.
interesting_fact: He holds three LSE degrees: a BSc in economics (1968), an MSc in logic and scientific method (1970) and a PhD in philosophy (1974). He is also a trustee of the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton.
deep_cut_fact: His PhD in philosophy at LSE was supervised by the famous philosopher of science Imre Lakatos, and he worked in the philosophy of economics before turning to the family business.
notes: Very private. The input Forbes bio appears to mix up names ('John and Margarita'); verify before quoting it. The foundation site warns about fraudulent emails that impersonate it. His Geneva family office (SETE SA) was named in a 2024 Swiss probe; per SETE he was not charged. Avoid this in outreach.

name: Miriam Baumann-Blocher
current_role: Owner and CEO, Läckerli Huus AG (Basel confectioner); shareholder in Ems-Chemie
profile: A food engineer (ETH Zurich) and daughter of Swiss politician and Ems-Chemie owner Christoph Blocher, she received an Ems-Chemie stake in 2004 when her father joined the Federal Council. She later sold most of it to her sisters. In 2007 she bought Basel's Läckerli Huus (founded 1904) and still runs it, with production consolidated in Frenkendorf.
interesting_fact: She tells Swissinfo that Läckerli Huus products contain no hidden sugar and that its Läckerli are sweetened mainly with honey. About 10% of sales come from outside Switzerland, mostly Germany and Japan.
deep_cut_fact: At 32, while researching companies to work for, she wrote to Läckerli Huus owner Mr. Klein. When he offered her the CEO job, she replied she would take it only if she owned the company, and he sold it to her. Her grandmother had given her Basel Läckerli every Christmas.
notes: Gives interviews about Läckerli Huus as an entrepreneur (Swissinfo, BaslerIN, Promarca). Best route is via Läckerli Huus. Keep the angle on entrepreneurship, not family politics.

name: Howard Butt III
current_role: CEO and board member, H-E-B (since 2021); board member, H.E. Butt Foundation
profile: Great-grandson of H-E-B founder Florence Butt and nephew of chairman Charles Butt, Howard Butt III succeeded his uncle as CEO of the family-owned Texas grocer in 2021. H-E-B has 455 stores in Texas and Mexico, about 160,000 employees and roughly $50 billion in sales. In 2025 he picked COO Roxanne Orsak as the company's first female president, starting in 2026.
interesting_fact: H-E-B gives 5% of pretax profits to charity each year. The company was started in 1905 by his great-grandmother Florence Butt.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming CEO he ran H-E-B's Mexico division (as of 2016). His father, Howard E. Butt Jr., co-created the Laity Lodge retreat center in the Texas Hill Country in 1961.
notes: Keeps a low media profile. The news@heb.com address came from a search snippet of an H-E-B page that loads by JavaScript, so I could not confirm it directly; check before use. H-E-B says media inquiries go to regional Public Affairs offices.

name: Wang Yi
current_role: Listed by Hurun alongside Liang Qin as co-holder of the Yangjie Technology fortune; exact role at the company unconfirmed
profile: Hurun lists Wang Yi with Liang Qin as owners of the Yangzhou Yangjie Electronic Technology (300373.SZ) fortune. Yangjie is a power-semiconductor maker that Liang Qin founded in 2000 and chairs. She is its sole disclosed actual controller, and its 2025 filings do not name Wang Yi, so his link to the company (likely family) is unverified.
interesting_fact: Yangjie Technology began in 2000 as a semiconductor brand-distribution business started by Liang Qin with about ten partners. It has since become a listed power-semiconductor (diodes, MOSFETs, SiC) manufacturer, a supplier to energy and EV-related markets.

public_contacts.value: zjb@21yangjie.com (Yangjie Technology, published in its 2024 ESG report; phone 0514-80889866)

notes: The name is ambiguous: 'Wang Yi' is also China's foreign minister, so do not confuse them. I could not confirm who this Wang Yi is. Yangjie's filings name only chairwoman Liang Qin as actual controller. Contact Yangjie via its published company email and confirm the relationship before any outreach.

name: Gerard Louis-Dreyfus
notes: Deceased: Gérard (William) Louis-Dreyfus, Louis Dreyfus Energy Services chairman and Louis Dreyfus Group heir, died 16 September 2016. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%A9rard_Louis-Dreyfus

name: Edmond Safra
notes: Deceased: Lebanese-born banker Edmond J. Safra (Republic National Bank of New York, Safra Republic Holdings) died 3 December 1999 in Monaco. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmond_Safra

name: Woo-choong Kim
notes: Deceased: Kim Woo-choong, founder and chairman of Daewoo Group, died 9 December 2019. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Woo-choong

name: Joseph Y Bae
current_role: Co-Chief Executive Officer and director, KKR & Co. Inc. (co-CEO since 2021)
profile: Joseph 'Joe' Bae joined KKR in 1996 after working as an analyst in Goldman Sachs' principal investment area. He built KKR's Asia-Pacific franchise from Hong Kong and later oversaw its infrastructure and energy real-asset portfolio. He became co-president in 2017 and co-CEO with Scott Nuttall in 2021, succeeding founders Kravis and Roberts. His fortune comes from his KKR stake.
interesting_fact: He co-founded and sits on the board of The Asian American Foundation, and he is a Fellow of the Harvard Corporation, Harvard's senior governing board.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2019 interview he recalled his father, a chemist, driving him an hour to piano lessons after work, recording each lesson and replaying it on the drive home. A 1996 NYT profile said he still slept on the futon he had at Harvard.
notes: Strong podcast fit: KKR is a major investor in infrastructure, energy and data centers, and Bae speaks regularly at events such as the Milken Global Conference. Route requests through KKR media relations.

name: Liang Xinjun
current_role: Principal of XIN Family, his Singapore single-family office (founded 2019); former vice chairman and CEO of Fosun International
profile: Liang Xinjun (b. 1968, Taizhou, Zhejiang) co-founded Fosun with Guo Guangchang in 1992. As vice chairman and CEO he helped build it into a conglomerate spanning steel, mining, tourism and pharmaceuticals. He resigned in 2017, cashed out his stakes and now invests from Singapore through XIN Family, including early-stage tech deals.
interesting_fact: He and Guo Guangchang were both young Fudan University staff when they started the business in 1992 that grew into Fosun, one of China's largest privately run conglomerates.
deep_cut_fact: He was Taizhou's top science scorer (理科状元) in the 1987 gaokao. He entered Fudan's highly selective genetic engineering department and won the top scholarship every year.

public_contacts.value: Milken Institute Asia Summit 2023 speaker profile (public appearance record)

notes: Low profile since 2017; he cited health reasons for leaving Fosun, so avoid that topic. He has spoken at Milken Asia Summit, which could be a warm route. No published XIN Family email found.

name: Peter Preben Wilhelmsen
current_role: Principal/co-owner, Awas Holding (parent of the Oslo family investment group Awilhelmsen), per Forbes
profile: Per Forbes, he is an heir of the Norwegian Wilhelmsen family that co-founded Royal Caribbean in 1968 and remains one of its largest shareholders. He co-owns the family business through Awas Holding, inherited after his father Arne Wilhelmsen died in 2020. The group invests in cruise, real estate (Linstow, active in Norway and the Baltics), offshore and financial assets.
interesting_fact: The family group (founded 1939 by shipowner Anders Wilhelmsen) financed its diversification with earnings from the tanker Wilstar, delivered in 1967. A year later it helped found Royal Caribbean.

public_contacts.value: https://www.awilhelmsen.no/contact (Awilhelmsen AS, Beddingen 8, Aker Brygge, Oslo; office tel +47 22 01 42 00)
post@linstow.no (Linstow, family real-estate company; general address)

notes: Very private; almost no public footprint beyond rich lists. Awilhelmsen's site names Arne Alexander Wilhelmsen as chairman and Arve Ree as CEO, and lists owners as Bent Christian Wilhelmsen, Arne Alexander Wilhelmsen and Paweco Trusts. Peter is not named, so his exact role is unverified. Best route is the Awilhelmsen office.

name: Guo Wengui
current_role: Federal prisoner. Sentenced in Manhattan on 29 June 2026 to 30 years for racketeering, wire and securities fraud. Former founder of Beijing Zenith (Zhengquan) Holdings.
profile: Guo Wengui (Miles Guo) was a Chinese real-estate developer (Beijing Zenith/Zhengquan Holdings) who fled to the US in 2014 and became a vocal critic of Beijing. A New York jury convicted him in July 2024 of defrauding online followers of hundreds of millions of dollars. In June 2026 he got 30 years and an $889M forfeiture order.
notes: NOT SUITABLE FOR OUTREACH: he is serving a 30-year federal sentence for fraud (source: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/30/chinese-billionaire-guo-wengui-gets-30-years-in-us-prison-for-huge-fraud). He is also wanted by China via an Interpol Red Notice. His rich-list wealth figure (Hurun 2014-2017) is obsolete.

name: Alec Gores
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, The Gores Group (Los Angeles/Boulder private equity firm)
profile: Born in Nazareth in 1953, Alec Gores emigrated to Flint, Michigan at 15. He built a computer-distribution business and in 1987 founded The Gores Group, which has bought or invested in 130+ companies, often corporate carve-outs. Since 2015 he has sponsored more than a dozen SPACs that took companies like Luminar, UWM, Hostess, Matterport and Polestar public.
interesting_fact: After immigrating at 15, his first job was bagging groceries for 25 cents an hour at his uncle's store in Flint, Michigan. His brothers are Tom Gores (Platinum Equity) and Sam Gores (Paradigm Talent Agency).
deep_cut_fact: He was the first in his family to attend college (computer science, Western Michigan University) and quit a General Motors job within six months. In 1978 he founded Executive Business Systems with $8,000 from his father and sold it to Contel in 1986 for about $10M.

public_contacts.value: jchou@gores.com (Jennifer Kwon Chou, Intermediaries, Investors and Media Relations; tel 310.824.8050)

notes: Good fit for an entrepreneurship and energy/EV episode: Gores Guggenheim took Polestar public and Gores SPACs listed Luminar. Route requests through the Gores Group media contact. Avoid personal-life topics.

name: Li Dongsheng
current_role: Founder and Chairman, TCL Technology Group / TCL Industries (chairman since 1996)
profile: Li Dongsheng (Tomson Li, b. 1957, Huizhou, Guangdong) joined TCL's predecessor TTK straight out of university in 1982. He became chairman and CEO in 1996 and built TCL into a global consumer-electronics, display (TCL CSOT) and solar-wafer (TCL Zhonghuan) group. His wealth comes mainly from his TCL Technology stake. He is also a vice chairman of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce.
interesting_fact: In 2004 TCL formed a TV joint venture with France's Thomson and bought Alcatel's handset business. That year Fortune named him Asia's Businessman of the Year, Time/CNN listed him among the 25 most influential global business people, and France awarded him the Légion d'honneur.
deep_cut_fact: He studied radio technology at South China Institute of Technology (class of 1982) and began as a technician at TTK Home Appliances, the joint venture that became TCL. He has written two books: 'Blue Ocean Transformation: TCL and Me' (2009) and 'Xiang Sheng Er Sheng' (2017).

public_contacts.value: ir@tcl.com (TCL Technology board secretary office; tel 0755-3331 1666)

notes: Strong energy fit: TCL Zhonghuan is a major solar-wafer maker. He is a National People's Congress deputy. Wikipedia also has a different Li Dongsheng (a former public-security vice minister jailed in 2016), so do not confuse them. He posts on Sina Weibo.

name: Huang Shan
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Fortune Trend Technology Co. (688318.SH, maker of TDX/Tongdaxin trading software)
profile: Huang Shan, a Wuhan University graduate (b. c.1962), has run the Tongdaxin (TDX) family of financial-software companies since the mid-1990s. He has chaired Shenzhen Fortune Trend since 2010. Its TDX market-data and trading terminal is used by most Chinese brokerages. The company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020 and his fortune comes from his controlling stake.
interesting_fact: Fortune Trend's Tongdaxin software is reported to be used by more than 90% of China's securities firms, so much of Chinese retail stock trading runs on a terminal his company built.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in 1995 as GM of Shenzhen Tongdaxin Communication Electronics, and he went on to run Tongdaxin entities in Wuhan, Shanghai and Beijing. In 2025 Fortune Trend's board approved a RMB 10 million donation to his alma mater, Wuhan University.

public_contacts.value: tdx@tdx.com.cn (Fortune Trend board secretary / securities office; tel 0755-83021794)

notes: Very low public profile and rarely interviewed. Forbes says the company listed in Shenzhen, but it actually trades on Shanghai's STAR Market (688318). Do not confuse it with the brokerage-software firm Compass/指南针. Board secretary is Tian Jin'en.

name: Wilfred Wang
current_role: Member of the Formosa Plastics Group family Management Center (管理中心); former chairman of Formosa Petrochemical Corp.; reportedly stepping back from group operations
profile: Wilfred Wang (Wang Wen-chao) is a second-generation member of Taiwan's Formosa Plastics Group family, a son of co-founder Wang Yung-tsai, and his fortune comes from family stakes in the group's listed companies. He chaired Formosa Petrochemical, which runs the Mailiao refinery complex, and joined the family Management Center in a 2017 succession restructuring. 2025 reports say he is gradually withdrawing from operations.
interesting_fact: As chairman of Formosa Petrochemical he ran Taiwan's privately owned oil refiner, the operator of the giant Mailiao complex. This energy and petrochemicals background fits the podcast's energy theme.
notes: Private; rarely gives interviews. Hurun lists him under China, but he is Taiwanese. He resigned as Formosa Petrochemical chairman in 2011 after refinery fires, so avoid that topic. A June 2025 GVM report says he dropped off the Forbes Taiwan 50 list. Contact via Formosa Plastics Group corporate channels.
